change: A workspace's 2048 MiB at boot (`memory=2048 plugged=0`) instead of 128 plugged to 2048 through virtio-mem during the boot (#561)
phase: the plug and the onlining of 2048 MiB on the one vCPU while the boot runs; separate runs read −15 nested and −8 metal (v20261122.06, labs 45074465204, 45074579100, 45074680619, 45078339515), so the ceiling is ~15 ms. Prior art: the kernel onlines hotplugged memory strictly in sequence, one memory block after another, and deferred struct page init, which spreads the boot's own memory over threads, does not apply to it (David Hildenbrand on linux-mm, [lore](https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/87v9disj2s.fsf@oracle.com/T/)). Squeezy (arXiv 2411.12893, 2024) measured virtio-mem's operations in seconds at GiB sizes and found init_on_free slows a plug. Neither measured a boot. The kernel has init_on_alloc and init_on_free off
decided_by: `ssh-first`, the two shapes as two trees of one run (`--opt` on a tree), 40 a side on bench and on bench-metal, `restore-first` beside them; 3 ledgers of each shape for the onlining's CPU
